title: Index Funds & Passive Investing
description: How to beat 90% of professional traders doing absolutely nothing.

slides.title: The Brutal Truth
slides.content: Statistically, over a 10-year period, 90% of professional Wall Street fund managers fail to beat the overall market average (the S&P 500).

slides.title: The Index Fund
slides.content: An index fund is an ETF or mutual fund that simply buys everything in the S&P 500. It doesn't try to be smart or predict the future. It just matches the market.

slides.title: Dollar Cost Averaging
slides.content: The ultimate strategy: Auto-invest $100 into an S&P 500 Index Fund every week, regardless of if the market is up or down. Over decades, compound interest will make you wealthy.

options.text: A fund run by an active manager who constantly trades
A passive fund designed to perfectly track a market index like the S&P 500
options.explanation: Index funds don't pick winners; they just buy everything.

options.text: A secret fund only for billionaires
Investing a fixed amount of money on a regular schedule, ignoring short-term price changes
options.explanation: DCA removes emotion and timing from investing.

options.text: Only investing when the market crashes
Selling all your stocks to average out your losses

quiz.question: True or False: Most active professional fund managers beat the S&P 500 over a 10 year period.

options.explanation: Very few professionals beat the passive index over a long timeframe.
